title: OSHA Fixed and Portable Ladder Checklist (29 CFR 1910.23)
subtitle: Use before a ladder's first use each shift and on routine site walks.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.

If a ladder has a structural or other defect, tag it "Dangerous: Do Not Use" (or similar wording) and keep it out of service until it is repaired or replaced (1910.23(b)(10)). If a use or setup item fails, correct it before the ladder is used.
Fall protection for employees on fixed ladders is set by 29 CFR 1910.28 and 1910.29 and is not covered by this list.

sections.title: All ladders: condition, spacing and tagging
items: With the ladder in position for use, every rung, step and cleat sits parallel and level, with even gaps.
Centerline gap between rungs measures 10 to 14 in. Elevator-shaft and telecom-tower ladders follow (b)(2)(i) and (b)(2)(ii).
Portable ladders 11.5 in or wider. Fixed ladders 16 in or wider (this figure applies before a ladder safety system is fitted).
No paint or other coating that could hide cracks or other structural defects.
Made of corrosion-resistant metal or has a protective finish against rust.
No surface that could puncture or lacerate the climber.
Ladder checked for visible defects before its first use this shift, and again whenever conditions call for it.
Any ladder with a defect carries a "Dangerous: Do Not Use" (or similar) tag and stays out of service until repaired or replaced.

sections.title: Climbing and portable ladder use
items: Ladder used only as its design intends, with no improvised uses.
Workers face the rungs going up and coming down.
At least one hand on the ladder throughout the climb.
No one climbs carrying an object or load that could throw them off balance.
Total load (weight and force) of the worker and all tools, equipment and materials carried is within the ladder's maximum intended load.
No moving with a worker on it
Nobody is on the ladder when it is moved, shifted or extended.
No one standing on the cap or top step.
Ladders or sections are not tied or fastened together for extra length unless specifically designed for that use.

sections.title: Portable ladder equipment and setup
items: Rungs and steps are corrugated, knurled, dimpled, skid-coated or otherwise treated against slipping.
Metal spreader or locking device holds front and back sections securely open during use.
No portable single rail ladder in use.
Feet on a stable, level surface, or the ladder is secured or stabilized against displacement.
In a passageway, doorway or driveway, the ladder is secured or barricaded off, for example with cones or caution tape.
A ladder used on a slippery surface is both secured and stabilized.
Both side rails bear at the top of a non-self-supporting ladder, unless it has a single support attachment.
Side rails reach 3 ft (0.9 m) or more above the upper landing surface being accessed.
Not stood on boxes, barrels or other unstable bases to gain height.

sections.title: Fixed ladders
items: 7 in (18 cm) or more from the rung or grab bar centerline to the closest fixed object behind. Elevator pit ladders need 4.5 in (11 cm).
Grab bars do not stick out past the rungs on the climbing side.
Through or side-step ladder rails rise 42 in (1.1 m) or more over the landing or access level. For parapets, see (d)(4)(i) and (d)(4)(ii).
No rungs in the extension. Rails flared to 24–30 in of clearance, or no more than 36 in with a ladder safety system.
Grab bars stand 42 in (1.1 m) higher than the landing they serve.
Hatch cover opens with enough clearance for easy access to or from the ladder. Counterbalanced covers open to 70 degrees or more from horizontal.
Rungs built so feet cannot slide off the ends.
Through ladders: 7–12 in to the structure edge. Side-step ladders: 15–20 in to the platform access points.
15 in (38 cm) clear on each side of the centerline.
30 in (76 cm) clear on the climbing side, or 24 in (61 cm) at an unavoidable obstruction fitted with deflector plates.

sections.title: Mobile ladder stands and platforms
items: Steps 16 in (41 cm) wide or wider.
Steps and platform have a slip-resistant surface, built in or added (dimpling, knurling, coating, tape).
Handrails 29.5–37 in (75–94 cm) high from the step's front edge, or chains or gates in special-use applications.
Work surface no higher than four times the shortest base dimension, unless outriggers, counterweights or similar stabilizers are fitted.
Units on wheels or casters have a system to impede horizontal movement while someone is on the unit.
Unit stays put while anyone is on it.
Handrail 36 in (91 cm) or higher on three sides. Midrail and toeboard where the top step is 20 in or more front to back.
Handrails 36 in (91 cm) or higher plus midrails in the platform area, or chains or gates in special-use applications.
Guardrails and toeboards on every exposed side and end.

references: 29 CFR 1910.23: Ladders (Part 1910 Subpart D, Walking-Working Surfaces)
Fall protection for fixed ladders: 29 CFR 1910.28 (duty) and 1910.29 (system criteria)
